summary: Device GUID collision after depot re-image causing Intune policy oscillation and enrollment churn
description: Summary: Several machines returned from depot repair this week end up re-enrolling into Intune with the same device GUID as an existing active asset. Impact: affected endpoints repeatedly toggle between 'Managed' and 'Pending' states, receive conflicting configuration policies, and surface multiple duplicate records in asset DB. This is causing user disruption (VPN and cert profiles failing) and extra manual work for IT to cleanup duplicates.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Depot team performs hardware replacement and re-imaging using the standard golden image build (autounattend + SCCM task sequence),
2) Device boots, OOBE completes, Intune enrollment triggers,
3) Device appears in Intune with a Device GUID that is already present for a different serial/asset tag,
4) Intune policy assignment flips between the two records and device state cycles between 'Enrolled' and 'Pending'
5) Observe duplicate entries in asset-db and ticket churn as VPN profiles fail intermittently.
observed_behavior: Newly imaged devices sometimes register with an existing GUID value in our MDM, leading to duplicated Intune records and oscillating policy application. Affected devices show intermittent 401/5xx for cert provisioning and fail conditional access checks.
expected_behavior: Each re-imaged device should generate a unique device GUID and create a single stable Intune enrollment record tied to the correct serial/assettag.
investigation_notes: 03/10: Repro attempted with local lab unit; observed GUID reuse when golden image included a stale provisioning package that embeds a hw GUID file.
03/11: Found that sysprep in our build pipeline was not regenerating the device identifier on images produced during certain depot-only runs (different build stamp from CI builds).
03/12: Cross-checked asset tagging and serial numbers; physical serials are unique and unchanged — collision only at MDM GUID level.
Hypothesis: depot deployment job re-applies a cached pre-provisioned registry key (HKLM SKU\DeviceID) from a cached image layer, leading to duplicate GUIDs on machines imaged from that layer.
actions_taken: 03/11: Paused depot batch imaging for machines targeted to US-East until root cause identified.
03/12: IT ran a remediation script on 12 affected devices to delete local provisioning GUID and re-trigger Intune enrollment (successful for 9 of 12).
03/13: Imaging pipeline patch submitted to regenerate device ID during finalize step (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/it-depot-scripts/pull/812).
Temporary workaround: manual GUID reset + force sync in Intune for returning users; instructed depot team to use 'freshize' job which runs sysprep with -generalize flag.
next_steps: 1) Merge and deploy the imaging pipeline fix that ensures sysprep runs with the correct parameters and clears cached provisioning values (target: 2026-03-15).
2) Run a one-time inventory reconciliation job to merge duplicate Intune records based on serial/asset tag and retire stale GUID entries.
3) Add an automated validation step in depot acceptance tests to verify generated device GUID uniqueness before releasing images.
4) Communicate guidance to depot vendors to avoid using cached image snapshots that contain pre-provisioned registry keys.
